explanation: Fires at the token that opens a finite full-verb predicate, not at its subject: strongest (above a quarter of max) on French semi-auxiliaries that take a bare infinitive ('Il doit', 'Elle peut', 'Il va'), on Indonesian auxiliaries ('harus', 'akan', 'dapat'), on a rate/duration adverb standing between the subject and a change-of-state verb ('the hurricane slowly weakened', 'the storm steadily strengthened'), and on the first subword of a finite lexical verb in narrative prose ('quenched', 'roared'). It stays below a quarter of max on a pronoun followed by the copula or a light verb ('he is', 'it is', 'il est', 'they are') - that is where its mirror pole fires - and also on plural-pronoun subjects, on plain English modal plus infinitive ('He must come', 'can be examined'), and on a base-form verb after a negated auxiliary ('did not quench').
